messages:
alex: Heads up — seeing an uptick in GPU Xid errors on a small slice of capacity after last week's kernel + driver refresh. Started 02:10 UTC. Noticing both ECC warnings and Xid 13/86 spikes on a few hosts.

maria: Which kernel/driver combo did we push?

alex: Kernel 6.4.12 + nvidia-driver 535.60 (packaged by infra image pipeline). Canary was green for basic perf tests but we didn't run long-running ECC burn.

cheng: Can you paste a sample dmesg?

alex: Sure — here's a recent excerpt from node gpu-prod-12: ```
[2025-11-02T02:13:41Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 86, PID=4321, GPU=0
[2025-11-02T02:13:41Z] kernel: nvidia: GPU0: GPU reported ECC memory error
[2025-11-02T02:13:42Z] NVRM: gpu: Runlist timeout on engine 0x04
```

will: Xid 86 usually points to thermal/ECC or firmware mismatch. Any ECC scrubbing alarms in telemetry?

alex: Yes — beyond the Xid lines, our cluster telemetry shows ECC corrected error counts jumped ~40% on the impacted hosts from 01:45–03:00 UTC. Other hosts same pool stable.

maria: Region/instance type?

alex: eu-west-1, p4d-type machines (3 hosts affected across two racks). We locked down other racks and traffic is routed away via the autoscaler but we still want a root cause.

cheng: Proposed plan: 1) Quarantine the 3 nodes (drain + cordon). 2) Run a firmware-only canary on 1 isolated spare with targeted mem-stress + ECC scrub for 2 hours. 3) If repro, test driver rollback on a spare. 4) If not repro, reimage the affected hosts and rejoin.

will: I can take node gpu-prod-12 for the firmware canary now. Need the exact commands and expected logs.

alex: Great — use the infra canary image + `nvidia-smi --query-ecc=bus,device,device_name,corrected_errors --format=csv -l 60` and run `memtester` container with 64GB stress for 2 hours. Watch dmesg for Xid. Example quick check: ```
# monitor
watch -n 10 nvidia-smi --query-ecc=corrected_errors --format=csv
# dmesg tail
journalctl -k -f | grep -i nvrm
```

oncall-bot: Incident policy: gpu-failure-monitoring triggered. Pager duty team notified.

maria: Also capture pstore and any GPU firmware versions: `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i firmware`. We need to compare with vendor recommended firmware for that kernel/driver.

cheng: Agree. If canary reproduces, we should test: a) alternate kernel (6.1 LTS) + same driver, b) same kernel + previous driver 525.x. That will help isolate kernel vs driver vs firmware.

will: Running canary now on spare gpu-canary-04 (eu-west-1). I'll post logs at 1765432600 when 30m in.

alex: Also flagging cost impact: draining 3 hosts reduces available capacity — autoscaler will spin up more nodes (higher on-demand spend). Keep finance looped if we hit >6h.

maria: Noted. Ops playbook — if rollback to 525.x reduces Xid rate we should schedule staged rollback for the entire rack with 15m stagger between hosts.

will: 30m update — no Xid after driver load sequence, ECC corrected errors stable so far. dmesg clean. Still running memtester.

cheng: If canary stays clean for 2h, reimaging might be next step for the 3 affected (possible bitflip in firmware flash path). If it repros, we'll run the kernel swap test.

alex: For traceability, please attach the canary job id and upload `journalctl -k`, `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q` and our ECC metric dump to the incident page. Link: https://redwood-internal/incidents/INC-2025-1479

will: Uploaded logs and vm snapshots at 1765432600. Canary still running. No new Xids.

maria: Thanks — good progress. If we stay green, next steps: 1) reimage gpu-prod-12, 2) run 2h mem stress, 3) join back to pool, 4) monitor for 24h. If any host fails, escalate to vendor support with full pstore and firmware blobs.

alex: I'll schedule the reimage window at 04:30 UTC if canary passes. Will ping again. :thumbsup:

will: Canary passed at 1765432680 — zero Xids during 2h test. Recommend reimage before full rollback.

cheng: Sounds good. After reimage, let's continue telemetry for 24h and mark the incident resolved if stable.

maria: I'll draft a short postmortem template and action items: canary baseline tests (add ECC long-run to our canary suite), add firmware compatibility matrix to runbook, and schedule quarterly firmware validation.

alex: Thanks team. Closing loop once reimages finish.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2025-1479 status -> monitoring.
